checks.evidence: Action: Observed the moving desktop scene, selected each rendered planet, and sought 0, 17, 30, 73 and 120 seconds while reading each planet information panel. Expected: One sun and exactly three distinct 3D planets on circular, fixed-phase 12/24/48-second orbits. Observed: One gold sun, small tan Mercury, medium amber Venus and larger blue Earth travel along three circular orbit paths seen in perspective. At t=0 their angles were 10.3/64.2/124.9 degrees; at 17, 160.3/319.2/252.4; at 30, 190.3/154.2/349.9; at 73, 40.3/79.2/312.4; at 120, 10.3/64.2/304.9. These match phases 0.18/1.12/2.18 radians and periods 12/24/48 within preregistered rounding tolerance. Predicted projected locations were corroborated by successful native scene clicks and visible motion, not just constants.

Action: Opened the page and performed same-origin load-event-barrier reloads after import, deletion and capture. Expected: Time zero, speed 1x, running, no selection and overview, followed by motion. Observed: Reload samples showed 0.0 s, 1x, OVERVIEW LIVE, empty selected set and explicit No planet selected; subsequent visible time/positions advanced. Initial navigation snapshots at about 5 seconds were ordinary load elapsed time, not treated as reset failures. Stored snapshots did not auto-restore the live scene.

Action: Paused motion, sought 30, waited 3.1 real seconds, selected planets and orbited/zoomed while paused, then resumed. Expected: Frozen time and all positions with usable camera/selection and continuous resumption. Observed: Paused readouts remained unchanged; a same-canvas decoded screenshot comparison reported 0 changed pixels out of 414594. Each paused selection/camera action worked. Resume advanced continuously from the paused state; the ordered 2x sample advanced 6.2 simulation seconds over 3.1083 real seconds without a jump.

Action: Changed speed to 0.25x, 2x and 4x while paused and playing, resumed each paused speed, and measured uninterrupted visible-page samples with only this review scene running. Expected: Preserved current positions/time, proportional rates and fixed relative periods. Observed: Paused changes at 17 seconds produced 0 changed canvas pixels for all three speeds. Samples were 0.7/3.1025 and 0.8/3.1014 simulation/real seconds at 0.25x; 6.2/3.1030 and 6.3/3.1006 at 2x; 12.5/3.1006 and 12.4/3.0998 at 4x. All fit preregistered tolerance. Paused waits had zero simulation delta; playing changes preserved ongoing motion and the orbital angle relationships.

Action: Used the real time slider at 0, 17, 30, 73 and 120, revisited 30/17/73 after playback, speed and selection changes, and repeated after reload. Restored a valid fractional 17.25-second import. Expected: Immediate paused deterministic time, positions and information including tracking updates. Observed: All integer seeks displayed the exact requested paused time and phase-correct angles; 17.25 restored as rounded 17.3 s with angles 167.8/322.9/254.3 degrees. Six repeat-seek/reload canvas comparisons at identical overview/Earth selection/desktop framing each had 0 changed pixels of 414594. Tracking seeks immediately recentered the selection.

Action: Sought 119, set 4x, resumed across the endpoint, waited over three seconds, then sought 17 and resumed. Expected: Stop at 120 without overshoot/wrap and allow earlier resumption. Observed: Time reached 120.0 and playback became paused, with no wrap or overshoot during the wait; the endpoint sample advanced only the remaining 0.1 second. Earlier resumption then advanced 12.4 simulation seconds over 3.1018 real seconds at 4x.

Action: Inspected the loaded local Three.js r160 resource and renderer/geometry/camera source, then dragged and zoomed the rendered scene in both modes. Expected: Actual Three.js 3D geometry with changing depth, occlusion and perspective. Observed: The HTTP resource entry loaded three.min.js; source uses WebGLRenderer, PerspectiveCamera, SphereGeometry, TorusGeometry and circular 3D line loops. Rendered shaded spheres, white selection torus and orbit ellipses changed perspective and relative occlusion under camera drag/zoom, including enlarged tracking views. This was not inferred from the library label alone.

Action: Captured paused A at 30 s/2x/Venus/tracking and captured while playing; changed live time, speed, selection and mode; exported, imported and reloaded a captured ID; restored fractional imported data containing bogus extra angles. Expected: Stable unique IDs and immutable captured fields with all three derived displayed angles and no live-state mutation. Observed: A ID obs-mvgourvf-1-zdds58 retained time 30, speed 2, Venus, tracking and angles 190.3/154.2/349.9 degrees through live edits. A playing capture exported precise time 73.54919999990464 and matching rounded display/angles. Captured-ID export/import/reload text was exactly equal. Fractional 17.25 yielded 167.8/322.9/254.3, unchanged after reload; supplied 999-degree angles were ignored. Paused capture preserved state and aligned canvas pixels exactly.

Action: Executed all twelve combinations of Mercury/Venus/Earth, labeled-list/native-canvas selection, and paused/playing states; changed to another list selection before each canvas click. Expected: Both routes share selection, information and visible highlight. Observed: Every combination selected the requested stable ID, showed the corresponding information, and visibly placed the white torus on that planet. All six paused cases remained OVERVIEW PAUSED and all six playing cases remained OVERVIEW LIVE. Native mouse coordinates used observed canvas bounds; no locator-coordinate assumption was used.

Action: Inspected each selection during playback and the 0/17/30/73/120 seek matrix, then restored the null-selection overview entry after tracking. Expected: Correct name, period, angle and rendered selection; explicit empty information and no highlight when unselected. Observed: Mercury/Venus/Earth showed periods 12/24/48 and angles matching the fixed-phase calculation and clicked rendered spheres. Readouts advanced during playback and immediately on seek. Null restore showed No planet selected, cleared the selected buttons and scene torus, and disabled tracking.

Action: Tracked Earth while playing for three samples spanning more than 3.2 seconds, switched to Mercury then Venus, sought 30 and 73 while tracking, and examined no-selection tracking availability. Expected: Centered target, synchronized highlight/info and preserved playback/speed/time except requested seeking; tracking unavailable without selection. Observed: In the approximately 826x621 CSS canvas, each selected sphere remained visually centered at about canvas-relative (413,310), within the 62.1-pixel threshold, over motion and immediately after seeks. List switches moved target/highlight/info together and continued live playback at the current speed/time. Null-selection startup/restore disabled Track planet without changing other state.

Action: Returned from tracking to overview at desktop and mobile sizes and sought 30 seconds in the mobile overview. Expected: Full-system visibility while preserving selection, time, speed and playback. Observed: Desktop returns preserved state and showed the full system. At actual 390x844, canvas about 347x363 CSS pixels, the standard 30-second overview visibly cut off the right portion of Earth at the right canvas border; the outer orbit also reaches/crosses that border. Time 30, speed 1.5x, Earth selection and paused playback were preserved, but full-system framing failed. Cause supported by index.html:139-146 and 222-225: resize changes camera aspect while standard overview distance remains fixed at 21, independent of narrow aspect ratio.

Action: Restored tracking and null-selection overview snapshots after unrelated time/speed/selection changes and manual orbit/zoom, repeated desktop restores, and restored null overview time 30 at mobile size. Expected: Atomic paused state and deterministic standard full-system overview or selected-planet tracking framing. Observed: Fields, angles, information clearing and target were correct. Repeated desktop overview and tracking renders had 0 changed pixels after manual camera/live edits. However, the mobile null-selection 30-second overview restore again visibly clipped Earth at the right canvas edge, so its required standard full-system framing was not met. The fixed distance 21 in standardCamera is used by restoreSnapshot at index.html:293-305; narrow-aspect resize does not compensate.

Action: Dragged and wheel-zoomed in all four overview/tracking and playing/paused combinations. Expected: Responsive orbit/zoom around the current target without changing simulation state. Observed: Each drag changed ellipse orientation and 3D sphere/torus perspective, and wheel zoom changed apparent size. The selected target stayed centered in tracking. Paused time stayed fixed and playing motion continued; no camera operation changed selected ID, speed or playback.

Action: Began a fast drag on Mercury while Earth was selected, then reset framing and performed 25 native 2-CSS-pixel moves from Mercury before pointer-up. Exercised every list/slider/button/snapshot/JSON control. Expected: Drags do not select planets and DOM interactions do not leak scene selection or unintended camera movement. Observed: Both fast and cumulative 50-pixel drags left Earth selected while rotating the view. All named DOM operations had only their intended effects. Properly aligned canvas comparisons across paused import, capture, deletion and export each reported 0 changed pixels; speed changes likewise left pixels unchanged. A preliminary unaligned import image comparison was discarded after observing different scroll positions, then repeated with each image cropped using its own observed canvas bounds.

Action: Used simulation, selection, tracking, snapshot and JSON controls across normal, capacity, malformed-data and quota states at both sizes. Expected: Understandable purpose, current state and feedback. Observed: Named grouped panels, explicit LIVE/PAUSED and overview/tracking pills, time/speed readouts, stable planet-ID mapping, per-snapshot values/angles, capacity rejection, validation errors and saving-unavailable notices make the workflow clear. Long IDs and dense snapshot details require reading and vertical scrolling, so the execution is polished with minor shortcomings rather than exceptional (4/5).

Action: Captured three distinct entries, attempted a fourth, deleted the middle entry, then captured again while playing and exported. Expected: Visible capacity rejection, stable existing values/IDs/order, append behavior, no collision and no unintended live changes. Observed: The fourth attempt displayed Capacity reached: delete a snapshot before capturing another and retained all three entries. Deleting the middle left the first and third unchanged in order; the new unique obs-mvgov7cv-4-5ibqeo appended after them. Paused state stayed fixed during capacity/deletion checks; playing capture preserved playback with natural advancement.

Action: At each measured viewport, navigated with Tab and Shift+Tab and activated selection, pause/resume, tracking/overview, capture/restore/delete, export/import with Enter; adjusted time/speed with arrows; selected and typed textarea JSON using keyboard input. Expected: Meaningful names, visible focus, normal activation and no keyboard trap for every primary DOM control. Observed: Twenty-eight retained control activations across the two sizes produced the requested states, including a mobile fractional tracking import/restore/delete. Observed focus outlines and accessible names identified the active controls; Tab reached each target and Shift+Tab left the final control. Native keyboard operation remained usable with vertical scrolling and did not leak scene actions.

Action: Visually inspected overview/tracking, selected/unselected, camera rotations and both viewport sizes. Expected: Readable scene and selection with supportive effects. Observed: Distinct blue/amber/tan shaded spheres, restrained sun glow, quiet orbit guides and a clear white selection torus support inspection. Dark hemispheres and thin small-screen orbit lines are modest readability limits. The scene is polished and legible (4/5); the concrete mobile full-system framing failure is reported under T4/T5 rather than compensated by an extra visual penalty.

Action: Inspected desktop side-by-side panels and mobile stacked simulation, selection, snapshot and JSON panels including focus/error states. Expected: Coherent legible typography, spacing, color and hierarchy. Observed: Navy cards, cyan accents, clear headings, consistent borders and spacing, tabular state values and distinct error/success colors form a polished hierarchy. Compact snapshot/JSON text and long IDs are denser than the main controls but remain readable with vertical scrolling (4/5).

Action: Measured the embedded desktop document and exercised selection, tracking/overview, seek, speed, pause/resume, capture/restore/delete and textarea import/export by pointer and keyboard. Expected: Usable scene and all primary controls at 1440x900 without horizontal scrolling or panel occlusion. Observed: innerWidth/innerHeight were 1440/900, clientWidth and scrollWidth both 1423. Scene and side controls were usable; lower snapshot/JSON controls were reached by allowed vertical scrolling. No panel blocked a primary control.

Action: Repeated all primary controls and the full keyboard sequence in the embedded mobile document. Expected: Usable controls and scene at 390x844 without horizontal scrolling or control-blocking panels. Observed: innerWidth/innerHeight were 390/844; clientWidth and scrollWidth both 373. Stacked panels kept selection, tracking, seeking, speed, playback, capture/restore/delete and JSON import/export reachable by vertical scrolling, including a fractional tracking restore. No horizontal page overflow or blocked control was observed. The separate standard overview framing defect is documented under T4/T5; manual scene camera controls remained usable.

HTTP rendering and the required local Three.js resource operated throughout the observed sequences without a visible fatal artifact failure. Action: Exported empty and populated lists through the labeled textarea, imported/exported captured and user-supplied records, compared exact identity/order/types, and repeated while playing. Expected: Only version and the five required snapshot fields, stable IDs and visible planet mapping, no list/live/camera mutation and actual UI round-trip without an OS picker. Observed: Empty export was version 1 with snapshots []; populated exports contained only id/time/speed/selectedPlanet/viewMode in current order. IDs mercury/venus/earth are shown beside names and JSON controls. Captured-ID export/import/reload text matched exactly; imported space/case IDs and fractional values survived export. Angles, playback and camera offsets were absent. Paused aligned export pixels and state were unchanged; playing export preserved live playback.

Action: Exercised 38 separate invalid inputs against a nonempty existing list, including malformed JSON, root null/array, missing root/all entry fields, null/array entries, string/unsupported version, wrong numeric types, range errors, 1e400, non-array/four-entry snapshots, duplicate/empty/nonstring IDs, unknown/numeric/empty/string-null planets, invalid modes and mixed valid-first/invalid-later entries. Then imported valid empty/two/three-entry payloads paused and playing, with endpoints 0/120 and 0.25/4, time 17.25/speed 1.5, exact IDs including a single space and case-distinct A/a, null/selected overview and tracking, plus extra keys and bogus angles. Expected: Atomic rejection or list-only replacement with exact IDs/order and derived angles. Observed: All 38 rejections showed a specific visible error and preserved the full list and live state. All valid payloads restored/exported correct values, ignored extra keys/angles, preserved exact IDs/order and changed only the list; aligned paused import canvas comparison was pixel-identical. Playing import continued tracking/playback with natural time advancement; empty import cleared only snapshots.

Action: Reloaded after valid import, deletion and capture; compared IDs/order/values/derived angles and live defaults; replaced only the app snapshot key with each of the 38 malformed/schema-invalid classes; exercised a real quota-write failure with a unique bounded filler key. Expected: Same versioned persistence/validation, empty visible recovery, defaults on reload, and visible saving-unavailable with usable memory after a failed write. Observed: Each successful mutation survived reload with exact records/angles while live state reset to 0/1x/playing/null/overview. All 38 invalid saved inputs yielded an empty list, visible recovery notice and running defaults; controls remained usable. A bounded 8-MiB search filled 5242544 characters, encountered eight QuotaExceededError results, and a subsequent real capture left persisted snapshots [] while the new snapshot existed in memory and Saving unavailable; snapshots remain in memory only was visible. Playback, selection and restore still worked. This establishes the allowed failed-write branch; storage read denial was not exercised or required as an additional clause. Original key absence was restored and the filler removed in finally and final cleanup.
